My claim: raising the input increases lamp current until the supply and lamp resistance set the limit.

Saved comparison — NPN settled DC model.

First: Manual control; input 1 V; supply 5 V; base resistance 10000 Ω; lamp resistance 220 Ω; gain β 100. Region: active. Base current 30.0 µA; lamp current 3.00 mA; transistor voltage 4.34V; lamp power 1.98 mW; probe red collector − black emitter = 4.34V.

Second: Manual control; input 1.5 V; supply 5 V; base resistance 10000 Ω; lamp resistance 220 Ω; gain β 100. Region: active. Base current 80.0 µA; lamp current 8.00 mA; transistor voltage 3.24V; lamp power 14.08 mW; probe red collector − black emitter = 3.24V.

Changes (second − first): base current +50.0 µA; lamp current +5.00 mA; transistor voltage -1.10V; lamp power +12.10 mW. Same captured probe pair; probe-voltage change -1.10V.

One circuit setting differs: Input voltage: 1 V → 1.5 V. Displayed readings are rounded.

My reasoning: the two voltage drops still add to the supply. I can check each drop with the red and black probes.
